author: JayWalk
content: So it's been 24 hours or so and I have done a lot of reflecting on this situation.  I have significant money invested (that will take years to recover from) in the project and since the news dropped I have not really been that worried...and I SHOULD be.  Part of the lack of worry concerns me, but after thinking really hard about it, it's because I actually honestly believe in this project and think that it will work out.  It's a weird place to be in as I am not frivolous with money and have a family to look after.  I guess for one of the first times I see this as a cause that I can truly get behind and know that even if I personally can't contribute to a solution here know that we have gotten to place where the team has proven themselves and that there are many people out there that feel the same way...some with wallets WAY bigger than me.  I would actually be shocked if we don't have some positive news in the following weeks.  We need this project to succeed not because of financial reason, but for how it is trying to change the world (which it is trying to).

author: [EMP] jith blade
content: Back of the napkin and making a number of assumptions, dropping USDC prices on ships still doesn't make sense to me.  Even if we sell $1M of ships through a limited 80% discount program, which is debatable because you can get 90% off atm on other ships, we are giving up $4M later to take $1M now.   In terms of runway, at $2M per month, we are gaining two weeks with this move and giving up 2 months. 2 weeks is not gonna move the needle.  Also, we are introducing more supply into an already beaten up and oversupplied ship market with no utility at present time. So we will also put more downward pressure on ATLAS and yes the optics aren't great either for those who paid VWAP.  I want to and will support the raising of funds in any way that I can, but it needs to make sense as an investment.   CSS habs/land in a limited fashion, locked POLIS, other NFTs like crew or Magic Eden charm ships boost, reduction of marketing budget/personnel, slowing down UE5 dev all seem like better options, but I am sure the team is performing this analysis and maybe my assumptions are off somewhere.

author: SW4GN3R [STAR]
content:
Perhaps worth noting just a couple of key assumptions we're making surrounding the future economy within Star Atlas. It's important to emphasize that everyone here is incredibly early in the formation of this new government, economy, and digital society, and dynamics are likely to change considerably through time.

1. I won't make a statement on any expected future value of any of the items we have sold. We modeled pricing and availability using some assumptions on initial adoption and growth, but more importantly, surrounding the potential for those assets to participate in the early emission curve (read: subsidy) of ATLAS. In GAO 0, we sold out entirely. Obviously in GAO 1, we have not. At least at the present moment.

2. The ATLAS emission curve is finite. It is intended to be a bootstrapping mechanism for the economy itself. It generates/provides the initial value to participants as the ecosystem grows. It is entirely possible that the DAO votes to enact a perpetual or periodic inflation rate at the end of the curve, though that is not how it is defined today.

3. Personally, I do not believe every user within Star Atlas in the future will have an extractive mentality. Gaming is and will continue to be the primary attraction to Star Atlas, at least in the near to intermediate term. But the promise of the Metaverse will attract a diverse set of new users into the ecosystem with a wide variety of motives for participation.

4. Do not underestimate the utility of entertainment. People are willing to spend disposable income to create enjoyment for themselves.

5. Over a long enough time horizon, it will be entirely necessary for the Star Atlas economy to function as a real world economy. With producers and consumers. Particularly as the emission curve is exhausted, and we transition into a player-to-player economy. We're taking very early steps to introduce this concept with the introduction of crafting in SAGE and Showroom R3. The key point is understanding that there will be participants in Star Atlas that are happy to pay a fee for some commodity or service or experience that brings them joy. They will care less about 'P2E', and be happy to spend $5, $10, $100+ per month to participate in this digital world. Where Star Atlas is truly different, is that those transactions won't be owned by ATMTA. They'll be freely traded amongst the users. Some users will spend time to produce that content or those goods, and others will consume them. Naturally, we have built the model to allow for taxation of those transactions, which enables the DAO to effectuate change, pay for it's own development services (including perhaps to ATMTA), and otherwise evolve over time.

6. What I want to make excruciatingly clear, is that this model is not contingent on perpetual user growth. User growth is good, but the objective of the future is to balance the formula of producers against the consumers within the economy. It will come to equilibrium regardless, but where that fulcrum lies depends on balance of participants.

author: SW4GN3R [STAR]
content:
*edit: also adding, that as merchants, and real businesses enter our digital universe, they'll largely or at least initially be contributors to the value equation. They'll pay rents, or purchase land, advertising, and create experiences to attract customers in game. This was loosely touched on yesterday, but the idea that these merchants can use Star Atlas as a new web frontend for their ecommerce business is transformative. When we have substantial real commerce taking place in Star Atlas, it implies true value is being created.

This is how we reach sustainability.

So in my view it remains a bar that is set by the team and the economy balancing activities should aim to maintain this bar. Do you share this view?

author: [AEP] MoonMonger
content: I'd argue you're misinterpreting my comment surrounding the emission curve. I was not implying that value was defined based on SCORE lifecycle - which admittedly is already longer than it was intended. Rather, it is based, to the fullest extent possible, on the lifetime value we could calculate at the time we were structuring those tiers, inclusive of the full 8 year emission curve. Honestly, impossible to model all the way out, but we did have numbers for total initial ship inventory across all ships at the time we were releasing GAO 0, exclusive of crafting. Nevertheless, we're going to need to be dynamic. Bear in mind, all current phase ships also include crew and components, which will not be the case in the future. It will be more like configuring a new car at a dealership, in which every option/upgrade has a charge.  On the second point, you are correct. Future crafted supply is going to be managed by a number of levers, with the intent of maintaining some level of balance between supply and demand, after factoring for user growth and demand for ship classes. Naturally, there will be some lag in the data here, and to your point on volatility, I would certainly expect periods where demand outpaces supply, and vice versa.  And simply put, yes. We are locked in on our pricing model moving forward. At present, the intention is still to release increased quantity of initial inventory at the same/similar price levels for all new GAO phases to come in the future. The increased supply is to match user growth and demand. Bering in mind, all previous ship models can only be produced through crafting. So, to the extent demand is higher on a legacy model, players will own the rights to satisfy that demand.

author: 𝕘𝕣𝕚𝕤𝕥
content:
I really love this idea. I suppose the community will be divided.

I’ve shared this before—the story about Bezos letting early investors know there was a 70% chance he would fail—and I’m sure I can find a Reddit comment from last year that I always felt there was even less of a chance for SA.

Not after Breakpoint. I now am deeply emotionally connected. This is the first blockchain gaming project that I view as early SC. I just want to support the Team to bring this project to life.

I’m sorry if some of you don’t share this belief. It may sound stupid to you, but I’ll lay my cards on the table. I’ve burned 4k on Apex Skins (could have bought ships or Polis) and heirlooms. I am emotionally invested in this project. I don’t care if there’s a 5% chance of this succeeding. The game we would have is so enticing I’m willing to take the chance.

I don’t see this as a fun way to make some money. I just want to be in the universe that Star Atlas makes it and has the chance to change traditional and blockchain gaming forever.

For all we know a VC or fund doubts the community. Maybe watching as some (not all, I’m aware that many will opt out) continue to support SA despite what happened gives them the resolve to offer the Team support. 

Love you all, you do you. Every person here is supporting the project simply by being here and not walking away.

author: PG I BULK
content: We were having a debate on this. TBH I think that will depend on your play style/time.  I still think that a big fleet of very small ships will eventually be the maximalist option. i.e. if you are a min max performer then that will be the way to go. I assess this based on what we know about Crew:Mining effectiveness ratio.  However,  if you are not overly concerned about min/maxing and you only have a few hours to play every day, then I think a larger ship or ships is the way to go. My large ship can out work your small fleet in a short time period. But if youre playing for longer, you'll be able more profitable than my large fleet with a smaller, less expensive fleet over time.  I made a twitter post about this, but if you don't have all the time in the world to play, youll want to be as effective as you can in a limited amount of time (large ship/more expensive option).  If you have all the time in the world you can get away with many small ships (small ships/less expensive).  Essentially, what is your time in game worth to you?

author: Nick [OPCG]
content: I've been reading a lot of comments expressing a need for SA to push for layoffs, pay cuts, and other internal shifts for the purposes of making an attempt at "restabilizing" the project after the FTX debacle. While I, like most of you, am concerned with the development of the game and most importantly the protection of our investments, extreme solutions are never an answer to problems especially in unprecedented times. The crypto world is still unsure as to what the long term repricussions from FTX will be but hastly decision making often causes more bad than good. I think the SA team and leadership are some of best in the industry and appreciate some of the transparency they have provided given the times. Its not easy to lead, and navigate situations like this however, layoffs aren't going to do anything besides create a subpar end product. Why fire the staff who have gotten the project to this point, understand the vision, and are fully committed?  Its important to keep our eyes on the end goal, hurdles will come, the leadership and staff will get us through this, lets not lose sight.

author: danparkticaONI
content:
Happy to answer questions but it's best to ping me--I am trying to keep an eye on Discord but we are definitely on the busier side right now.  To address some points that I've seen come up:

- ATMTA, Inc. was formerly registered in Nevada as Automata, Inc.  In March, we moved to Delaware to optimize for a few reasons, in large part to be ready for prospective capital partners if/when the right opportunity arose due to the robustness of Delaware courts w/r/t corporations law.  We also implemented the name change then as well.

- We considered many jurisdictions while consulting with our legal (mainly Latham) and tax advisors (Deloitte).  Singapore was under consideration but we did not register there; we had a Panama entity but operations always were centered out of the US entity.  I want to emphasize that we have access to the best advisors in the business and we give great weight to their advice.  It was clear that the US was the best option for our operations.  We remain vigilant to the changing economic, legal, tax, and regulatory landscape around the world and believe the US still remains the optimal choice, but that may not be true forever.

- There's a older draft deck--note it is older & outdated but I believe remains materially accurate--that seems to have been circulating and it does go into ATMTA's 2021/2022 financials.  It should be clear from that data that ATMTA has been efficient in spending as much as possible on production / engineering--ATMTA's core objective.  For a AAA development we run on the lean side but have made significant progress on development regardless.  Note that the financials reflect the USD value of revenue even when a significant portion of the revenue was taken in as ATLAS, which has lost much of its value since.  Also note that the financials include opex numbers and don't show our tax figures--and we paid a significant amount in 2021 taxes.  Note that we also had to pay taxes on ATLAS taken in as income and we did not have an opportunity to offset the 2021 income.  ATMTA was able to take a far more tax optimized strategy in 2022 and should be able to do so on a go-forward basis.

author: danparkticaONI
content:
Also, the website atmta.com admittedly could use a makeover--it has been on our to-do list, it's just much lower priority than other development efforts.  Rest assured we are providing plenty of detail about the company, financials, the state of development, and future plans to potential capital partners (under NDA).  Those efforts and talks are ongoing.

In the meantime, product / engineering efforts are still full steam ahead.

author: Signal
content: Thanks @Lysimach | Make Polis Great! I would like to focus this on pure utility and access. As SCORE will not be available forever, ATLAS rewards in the future would have to come from everybody on board playing the game and operating each facility, generating their own yields. For me this is much better for mitigating any investment/SEC concerns.  So I would say 0 share in overall revenue BUT there is potential for huge benefits in game by having access to this ship. Jose mentioned on the brew a strategy such as finding very rare resources in the HRZ, so we fly the titan there and everybody on board has access to the planets for pretty low risk.   We could swap 'exclusive' access to certain parts of the ship, habs, commercial areas for tokens also.   I think many of us also like to see this as an alliance hub / ship for peace, cross guild, cross faction, anyone can own the token for access. I imagine if someone has paid for access they are unlikely to try and destroy it    I will not take up more space in this FR chat but we do have a public poll and discussion ongoing in The Club server, if you check my bio

author: Signal
content: Yeah the trouble with that idea, the whole “cut back on UE5” or even cut UE5 is that you have tons of stuff at various stages of development in a large studio like Sperasoft for instance that’s all maybe 20-50% done and becomes effectively worthless if you just tried to cut off the work.  So you actually WASTE millions by chucking all that out the window.  Also try laying off Sperasoft and ceasing UE5 development and thinking you’ll maintain the ability to hire them back under the same terms later.  Raising funds even if it means VCs and partnerships and rushing around is a much stronger path for now.  I sincerely think they’ll do this sale, release V2 and start up SAGE, and lock in multiple deals with gameplay live under better conditions.  At a minimum, what we are doing now has effectively stopped their burn.  We are buying them a burn free month or two while they launch all the goodies and negotiate with their partners.  30-60 extra days for them without burn really is a huge difference maker to their negotiating position.  We know what’s coming, so do they, they want to get it out there and that’s all we are really helping them do right now.

author: The Man | RomeONI
content: Solution brainstorming, as there is plenty of people pointing out problems (myself included). What could be done to make things work without overly hurting anyone involved? First thought I have for the claim stakes, as they were given out in large quantities already, multiply the supply being sold by ATMTA by a number (for my examples, 10). They could keep the same pricing listed, but it would be 10 packs of stakes. They would still come with the needed drills and plants when purchased in this sale. The existing supply would remain the same, but be a much smaller percentage of what is out there, while still benefitting the original poster holders. As claim stake mining numbers are not out yet, each stakes output could be adjusted with this knowledge before putting out the numbers for the claim stakes ability to mine. People who buy 10 packs but do not need all 10 could resell the extras on the market, generating marketplace sales tax, or hold onto them and be self-urged towards more ships to support the additional claim stakes. ATMTA would generate the same amount of revenue per direct sale as they forecast, although direct sales will be a bit smaller. Just a thought, and open to more constructive ideas.
